lines.text: Do you know how your phone knows which way is up?
You turn it sideways for a video, and the picture spins around with you. Nobody pressed a thing.
Look inside. Right next to the processor sits a chip smaller than a grain of rice.
Zoom in a thousand times. A little block of silicon, hanging on springs thinner than a hair.
All around it, rows of tiny fingers, almost touching. Like two combs pushed together.
Now tilt the phone. Gravity drags the block a tiny bit to one side, and the gaps change.
Smaller gap, more electric charge. The chip feels that hundreds of times a second.
So it knows exactly where down is, and turns the screen to match.
The same little weight counts your steps, and feels it when you shake it.
No magic. Just a tiny weight on a spring. Now you know!
